findings.title: Trace ID is no longer added to plugin request logs
findings.body: The previous LoggerMiddleware explicitly appended a traceID field from tracing.TraceIDFromContext to plugin request logs. After this refactor, LoggerMiddleware relies on contextual attributes added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, but instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, datasource name/UID, and user login. As a result, plugin request logs can lose trace correlation unless some other middleware independently injects the trace ID.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a throwaway logger
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of the receiver or a child logger that shares the same recorded Logs. Since LoggerMiddleware now emits logs via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), tests using this fake will record those messages on an unreachable object, making it impossible to assert logging behavior and allowing regressions to pass silently.

findings.title: No tests cover the new contextual logging middleware
findings.body: This PR moves request-scoped logging context into a new middleware and changes LoggerMiddleware to depend on that context, but the only test change is renaming the metrics middleware test. There is no coverage verifying that ContextualLoggerMiddleware injects the expected fields or that LoggerMiddleware emits them, so regressions in logging fields are likely to be missed.

findings.title: Metrics middleware mutates a shared instance when wrapping next
findings.body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates one MetricsMiddleware and the returned middleware function assigns imw.next = next each time it is applied. If the same ClientMiddleware is applied more than once, all returned clients share the same MetricsMiddleware and the last assignment overwrites the next handler. This can route requests through the wrong chain and creates a potential data race. A new middleware instance should be created for each next client.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to Logger is a breaking interface change
findings.body: The exported Logger interface now requires FromContext. Any external implementation of this interface will fail to compile after this change. Only the in-repo fake is updated, so if this package is consumed outside the repository this is an API break that should be called out or handled compatibly.
